source.title: Open problems originated in our research work with Zoltán Daróczy

accepted.question_text: Fix a non-integer q > 1, write θ = 1/q and k = [q], and let A_k = {0,1,…,k}. A function F:[0,1)→ℂ is additive with respect to the Rényi–Parry expansion if F(0)=0, ∑_{l≥1}∑_{a=1}^k |F(aθ^l)| < ∞, and for each x\in[0,1) one has F(x)=∑_{n≥1} F(ε_n(x)θ^n), where ε_n(x) are the digits of the regular expansion of x. Let t=t_1t_2⋯ be the quasi-regular expansion of 1, let G(z)=1-t_1z-t_2z^2-⋯, and call a continuous additive function elementary if it belongs to the closed linear span of the functions generated by sequences u_ν=ν^jρ^ν, where ρ is a root of G(z)=0 in |z|<1 and 0\le j<m-1 when m is the multiplicity of ρ. Is every continuous additive function elementary?

evidence.quote: Theorem 1. If F : I1 → C is a continuous additive function, then F (jθ n) = jF (θn) ( j ∈ A k, n ∈ N).
Such types of continuous additive functions, and even the elements of the closed space generated by such functions called to be elementary continuous additive functions, also.
We formulated our conjecture that every continuous additive function is elementary.

accepted.question_text: Let t=(t_0,t_1,⋯) with t_0=1 and bounded coefficients, let l_1 be the space of absolutely summable complex sequences b=(b_0,b_1,⋯), and let σ be the left shift. Define H_t={b\in l_1 : σ^l(b)\,t=0 for every l=0,1,2,⋯}. Let R(z)=t_0+t_1z+⋯, and for each root ρ of R in |z|<1 and each 0\le j<m-1, where m is the multiplicity of ρ, consider the sequences b_ν=ν^jρ^ν. Let H_t^(e) be the closure in l_1 of the finite linear combinations of all such root-generated sequences. Must one always have H_t^(e)=H_t?
accepted.context_brief: Subspace of l1 defined by shift relations

evidence.quote: Let H (e) t be the space of the finite linear combinations of such solutions, furthermore let H (e) t be the closure of H (e) t .
Conjecture 1. H (e) t = Ht.

With the same notation as in q_002, let R(z)=t_0+t_1z+⋯. If R(z) has no zeros in the open unit disk |z|<1, does it follow that the only sequence b\in l_1 satisfying σ^l(b)\,t=0 for all l\ge 0 is the zero sequence? Equivalently, is H_t={0} whenever R(z)
e 0 on |z|<1?
accepted.context_brief: Zero-free generating function and triviality of H_t

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. Assume that R(z) ̸= 0 in |z|< 1. Then Ht = {0}.

accepted.question_text: Let λ_1>λ_2>⋯>0 with L_N=λ_{N+1}+λ_{N+2}+⋯ and L_0<∞, and fix an integer k>0. Suppose {λ_n} is a smooth interval-filling sequence of order k, meaning every x\in[0,kL_0] has an expansion x=∑_{n≥1} ε_nλ_n with digits ε_n\in\{0,1,⋯,k\}, and there exists T with λ_{n+T}\le λ_n/2 for all n. Let F:[0,kL_0]	oℂ be a continuous additive function with respect to this expansion. If F is differentiable at one arbitrarily chosen point, must F(x)=cx for some constant c?

evidence.quote: We say that λn is an interval filling sequence of order k if each x ∈ [0, kL0] can be written as x = ∑∞ n=1 εnλn, where εn ∈ {1, . . . , k}(= Ak).
We say that {λn}is a smooth sequence if there exists an integer T for which λn+T ≤ 1/2 λn (n ∈N).

Conjecture 3. Let {λn} be a smooth, interval filling sequence of order k. Let F be a continuous additive function with respect to {λn}. Assume that F is differentiable in one arbitrary chosen point. Then F (x) = cx, c is a constant.

accepted.question_text: Let {λ_n} be a nonincreasing sequence of positive numbers with L_n=λ_{n+1}+λ_{n+2}+⋯<∞ for every n, and let H={x : x=∑_{n≥1} ε_nλ_n with ε_n\in\{0,1\}}. Assume H contains an interval. Suppose (a_n)\in l_1 has the property that for every choice of coefficients δ_n\in\{-1,0,1\}, the relation ∑ δ_nλ_n=0 always implies ∑ δ_n a_n=0. Must the ratio a_n/λ_n be constant for all n?
accepted.context_brief: Completely additive functions and interval-containing subset sums

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4. Let {λn}be a sequence of positive numbers for which λn ≥ λn+1 (n = 1 , 2, . . .) such that Ln = λn+1 + · · · < ∞. Assume that H = { x | x = ∑∞ n=1 εnλn, ε n ∈ { 0, 1} } contains an interval.
Assume furthermore, that {an}∞ n=1 ∈ l1 is such a sequence for which ∑ δnλn = 0 δn ∈ {−1, 0, 1} always implies that ∑∞ n=1 δnan = 0.
Then an/λn = constant (n = 1, 2, . . .).

accepted.question_text: Fix θ with 1/2<θ<1. Let F\subset\{-1,0,1\}^ℕ be a set of infinite sign sequences, and for each N let F_N be the set of prefixes δ_1,⋯,δ_N\in\{-1,0,1\}^N that can be continued to some element of F; write π_N(θ,F)=\#F_N. Suppose π_N(θ,F)	o∞ as N	o∞. If a=(a_1,a_2,⋯)\in l_1 satisfies ∑ ε_n a_n=0 for every ε\in F, must a_n/θ^n be constant?
accepted.context_brief: Large families of sign constraints in l1

evidence.quote: Let F be a set of sequences ε = ε1ε2 . . . , εν ∈ {− 1, 0, 1}. Let FN be the set of those sequences δ1, . . . , δN ∈ {−1, 0, 1}N which can be continued by suitable εν ∈ {−1, 0, 1}(ν = N + 1, N + 2, . . .) such that δ1 . . . , δN εN +1εN +2 · · · ∈ F . Let πN (Θ, F ) = #( FN ).
Conjecture 5. Let F be such a set of ε ∈ {−1, 0, 1}N, for which πN (θ | F) → ∞ (N → ∞). Let a = a1a2 · · · ∈ l1 be such a sequence for which ∑ εnan = 0 whenever ε ∈ F . Then an/θn = constant.

accepted.question_text: Fix 1<q<2 and write θ=1/q. For a parameter η\in[θ,θ^2/(1-θ)], define the level-η regular expansion of x by iterating the rule x=ε_1(x)θ+θx_1 with binary digit ε_1(x)=0 for x\in[0,η) and ε_1(x)=1 for x\in[η,qη). For η_1<η_2 in this interval, let H(η_1,η_2) be the set of points whose level-η_1 and level-η_2 expansions are identical. Must H(η_1,η_2) always have Lebesgue measure zero?

evidence.quote: Regular expansion of level η : Let x ∈ I(1) η . Then x = ε1(x)θ + θx1, ε 1(x) ∈ A 1, x 1 ∈ I(1) η ; ε1(x) = 0, if x ∈ [0, η) ; 1, if x ∈ [η, qη).

Conjecture 6. Let η1 < η 2, η1, η2 ∈ [θ, θL]. Let H(η1, η2) be the set of those x ∈ [0, L] for which their expansions of level η1 and of level η2 are the same. Then the Lebesgue measure of H(η1, η2) is zero.
